Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

TiDEomics 0.99.7

SIGNIFICANT USER-VISIBLE CHANGES

  • plot_scatter() now shows the dashed y = x line by default only when comparing same-named properties from two data frames. This can be overridden by show_diagonal.

  • DE_timecourse() uses clearer unified column names in result tables, the changes are summarised as below. fits and design retain the original model coefficient names.

    Test 0.99.6 result-column name 0.99.7 result-column name
    Factor time effect TimeFactor<time>, or logFC when two time points logFC_TimeFactor<time>
    Numeric time effect TimeNumeric in global_time_effect, or logFC in time_effect and reference_time_effect logFC_TimeSlope
    Spline time effect splines::ns(...)<basis> terms converted by make.names() SplineBasis_1, SplineBasis_2, etc.
    Factor group-time interaction GroupX.TimeFactor<time>, or logFC when one interaction delta_logFC_GroupX_TimeFactor<time>
    Numeric group-time interaction GroupX.TimeNumeric, or logFC when two groups delta_logFC_GroupX_TimeSlope
    Spline group-time interaction GroupX:splines::ns(...)<basis> terms converted by make.names() delta_SplineBasis_GroupX_1, etc.
    Group contrast at reference time GroupX_at_reference_time, or logFC when two groups logFC_GroupX_at_reference_time

    X represents a non-reference group; <time> represents a non-reference time level.

TiDEomics 0.99.6

NEW FEATURES

  • TiDEomics now supports multi-dataset / multi-omics analysis:
    • combine_tide() combines multiple prepare_tide() outputs, identifies features shared by the datasets, and returns all-feature filtered data, shared-feature subsets, and filtering summaries.
    • run_consensus_WGCNA() performs consensus WGCNA across datasets using the shared features.
    • extract_consensus_hubs() returns consensus and dataset-specific features with highest kME to their modules.
    • Examples and documentations now include a second simulated dataset to demonstrate the multi-dataset / multi-omics workflows.
  • Some existing functions now accept multi-dataset / multi-omics input:
    • plot_trend() supports multiple layouts for multi-dataset input, with shared or independent y-axis scales.
    • plot_pca() and plot_umap() calculate and plot per dataset using all available complete features or shared features, and combine the plots with shared legends.
    • plot_cor_matrix() plots correlation heatmaps per dataset side by side with shared legends, and reports pairwise correlations of cophenetic distances when samples are shared across datasets.
    • plot_modules_v() vertically stacks module heatmaps and mean profile views for multi-dataset input.
    • plot_modules_h() horizontally aligns module heatmaps and mean profile views for multi-dataset input, with the optional enrichment annotation on the right and shared legends.
    • summarise_module_metrics() accepts both individual and consensus WGCNA results, reporting metrics including kME distribution summaries.
  • New analysis and visualisation functions:
    • DE_timecourse() performs limma-based temporal differential-expression analysis within selected groups or jointly across groups.
    • plot_scatter() compares per-feature properties between datasets or within one table, with quadrant labelling and correlation summaries.
    • plot_upset_h() provides Upset plot of feature set intersections with optional horizontally aligned per-intersection enrichment textboxes.
    • plot_upset_v() provides Upset plot of feature set intersections with optional vertically aligned enrichment dot matrices with configurable dot size and colour, term ordering, and custom term colours.

SIGNIFICANT USER-VISIBLE CHANGES

  • Enrichment workflows now provide more consistent result structures. enrichR_list() reports feature counts. enrichGO_rank() follows enrichGO_list, returns full results under all and optionally adds simplified terms under simplified.

  • WGCNA workflows are improved. In addition to the multi-dataset / multi-omics compatibility, prepare_WGCNA() now reports a custom power estimate, and plot_modules_h() has improved display controls, including feature marking with custom colours, enrichment term wrapping, and selected module profiles.

  • prepare_tide() has filtering mode below_quantile renamed to quantile, and reports residual cutoffs.

  • decomp_variance() now reports numbers of evaluated features, including successes, errors, warnings, and skippings.

  • calc_feature_property() adds Net_FC, reporting signed abundance difference between last and first time points.

  • theme_custom() supports font family control.

BUG FIXES

  • plot_WGCNA() now plots dendrogram for every feature block.
  • prepare_tide() now accepts feature_threshold = NULL.
  • Enrichment legends in plot_modules_h() and plot_upset_h() now omit unused colours.
  • enrichGO_list() now omits universe when no background is supplied, rather than passing an explicit NULL to clusterProfiler::enrichGO().

TiDEomics 0.99.5

SIGNIFICANT USER-VISIBLE CHANGES

  • enrich_p_threshold renamed to enrich_threshold in plot_modules_h().
  • assay parameter in plot_modules_h() and plot_modules_v() now must be specified explicitly (no default).
  • prepare_WGCNA(): assay parameter must be specified explicitly (no default).
  • plot_trend(): ylab parameter renamed to ylabel, default changed from "Abundance" to "Log2 abundance".
  • plot_modules_v(): default ylabel changed from "Log2 abundance normalised to Time 0" to "Log2 abundance".
  • plot_cor_matrix(): default title changed from "Correlation between samples" to NULL; the title is now auto-generated as "Sample correlation (<Method>)" with the method capitalised (e.g. “Sample correlation (Spearman)”).
  • plot_pca() and plot_umap(): when circle = TRUE, auto-computed axis limits now use 0.35x padding around the data range (via coord_cartesian()) instead of 1.5x the min/max (via xlim()/ylim()).
